1. Strategy — Executive Product Vision

Product: IMR (Internal Mobility Request) — Part of Opportunities.epam.com

Core Value Proposition: "IMR" is a solution designed to simplify the entire relocation process for EPAMer. From start to finish, the product provides relocating people with the information, guidance, and support they need to navigate every step of the way. Our goal is to make EPAMer move easier, more efficient, and less stressful.

Problem Statement: Identify and describe in 2-3 sentences the specific problems or challenges within the organization that the product aims to solve. The lack of a centralized, standardized relocation solution leads to inefficiencies for both employees and Resource Managers, resulti

Vision: Articulate a clear and inspirational vision of what the product aims to achieve in the long-term. Include the unique features and capabilities of the product that are essential for solving the problem. Our vision is to make every EPAMer’s relocation journey seamless, efficient, and stress-free by providing a centralized hub for information, personalized guidance, and expert support. "IMR" will empower employees to confidently navigate every step of the process, track their progress, and access tailored resources, while enabling the company to standardize and scale relocation practices globally

Delivery Scope & Predictability Quality & Tech Debt Project Jira Reports

DeliveryⓘDelivery health at a glance: work-in-progress flow (CFD), throughput balance (Opened vs Resolved), and how long work takes to actually complete (Cycle Time) vs its total lifetime (Lead Time).

Cumulative Flow DiagramⓘA stacked area chart of Backlog, In Progress and Done over time. The vertical gap between adjacent bands is the work-in-progress (WIP); a widening band signals congestion, while a narrowing one signals flow. Flat 'In Progress' band = work is queued, not being done.

Opened vs Resolved (biweekly)ⓘCompares issues Opened vs Resolved in each 2-week bucket. When Opened persistently exceeds Resolved, the backlog grows (demand > capacity); the reverse means the team is burning down outstanding work.

Cycle TimeⓘCycle time = first 'Done/Closed' MINUS first 'In Progress' (from the issue changelog). Formula: avg(Done − In Progress) over completed STORY and TASK issues only (bugs have their own dedicated 'Cycle Time (Bug)' metric). It measures ONLY the active work duration — how long it actually takes to BUILD/complete a feature once started — and EXCLUDES queue/backlog wait. This is the 'how fast do we execute' metric. Compare with Requirements Cycle Time below, which measures the wait BEFORE work starts (In Progress − Created) and is usually larger.

27.0 days avg

Requirements Cycle TimeⓘTime from a requirement being CREATED to it ENTERING DEVELOPMENT (first 'In Progress' transition). Formula: avg(story_dev_start − story_created) for STORY/TASK items entering development in the period (requirements only — excludes bugs). Period = sprint, or 2-week bucket if sprints are absent. It measures how long a requirement WAITS before work starts (incl. backlog/refinement time). HEALTHY = < 1 sprint / 2-week period (<14 days), i.e. requirements don't sit unrefined for more than one iteration. Why it differs from Cycle Time: Cycle Time = Done − In Progress (active build time, all types); Requirements Cycle Time = In Progress − Created (wait time to start, story/task only) — so it is usually larger and reflects the backlog/refinement bottleneck.

Process Metrics - Trends

Metric

Y-axis: Requirements Cycle Time (days) · X-axis: period (sprint / 2-week bucket). Default shows the last 5 periods with project activity.

Scope & PredictabilityⓘHow much the team delivers and how predictably: throughput and velocity, backlog readiness, scope-change churn, and aging work. Together these reveal whether delivery is stable or slipping.

Throughput (completed per 2-week period)ⓘNumber of issues completed in each 2-week period (any issue type). Throughput is a raw capacity measure; velocity below is a filtered, more refined one.

Velocity (completed Story/Task/Bug per 2-week period)ⓘNumber of Story/Task/Bug issues completed per 2-week period. Velocity is the team's realized capacity and is the basis for forecasting how much can be committed in future iterations.

Average Velocity (2-week)ⓘThe mean of the per-period velocity values. A stable average supports commitment and forecasting; large swings indicate unpredictability.

9.8 /2wk

Backlog Health — Ready for DevelopmentⓘNumber of issues currently in the 'Ready for Development' state. A healthy backlog keeps enough groomed, ready-to-start work so the team never starves for input.

10 items

Sprint Scope StabilityⓘHow stable committed sprint scope is (added vs removed items). High instability means the team commits to work that is later dropped or expanded mid-sprint — a predictability risk.

N/A (no sprints)

Avg Scope Change Volume (changed issues)ⓘAverage number of changed Story/Task/Bug issues (at least one status transition) per period. Per sprint when sprints exist, otherwise per 2-week period. High churn indicates unstable requirements or poor upfront planning.

35.8 / 2wk

Scope Change Volume by 2-week period (changed issues)ⓘPer-period count of issues (Story/Task/Bug) that changed status AT LEAST ONCE — ANY transition (New→Open, Open→In Progress, In Progress→Resolved, ...). This is a BROAD 'churn' metric: it counts every issue that moved, including normal forward progress. Spikes show periods of heavy rework/scope drift; a flat low line reflects a stable pipeline. DIFFERENCE vs Requirements Rework Rate: Scope Change counts ALL status changes (any direction), while Rework Rate counts ONLY returns to requirements/refinement (New/Open/To Do/Backlog/Reopened/Analysis/Design/Ready for Dev) AFTER dev started. So Scope Change is always larger — it is a volume of movement, not a rate of rework.

8. Event-Driven Analytics

Advanced event analysis: defect causality (story status at defect birth, parent-child closure sync, sub-bug creation constraints), the impact of labels / custom fields on cycle time and rework, and the Jira Cross-Linkage & SDLC Waste classifier.

Story Status at Defect BirthⓘFor every Bug/Sub-Bug, the parent feature (Story/Task) is resolved via hard linkage: Sub-Bugs use the system parent field; Bugs use issuelinks (blocked-by / relates-to / associated / depends) to a Story/Task. The doughnut shows the parent's status at the exact second the defect was created (from the parent's changelog). Answers: 'in which phases do our stories generate bugs?'

Defects with a resolvable parent: 45 of 76

Sub-Bug Creation Constraints ValidationⓘFor every [Story/Task/Bug → Sub-Bug] pair, captures the parent's status at the exact second the Sub-Bug was created. Tests the hypothesis that Sub-Bugs are only created while the parent is in 'In Testing' (100%).

Is it true that a Sub-Bug is created only when the parent is in In Testing?

⚠️ Hypothesis REJECTED — Sub-Bugs are also created while the parent is in other statuses.

Parent-Child Closure Sync Tracker — Stuck ParentsⓘFor every parent (ANY issue type) with Sub-task / Sub-Bug children, computes T_last_child = max(updated) among children that reached Closed/Resolved. A parent is flagged as STUCK when it has NO status transition strictly after T_last_child — i.e. it did not advance to its next workflow status (in testing / resolved / closed / done / ...) once all its children closed. Latency = hours elapsed since the last child closed (still stuck).

Parents whose status did not change after the last Sub-task / Sub-Bug closed, even though their workflow (section 2) expects a move to the next status. 25 of 27 analyzed parents are stuck.

Jira Cross-Linkage & SDLC Waste DashboardⓘClassifies every issuelinks record across ALL issues (horizontal links, not just parent/child) into 4 macro-categories of SDLC waste. <b>A · Hard Blockers</b> (blocks / is blocked by / Depend) — links that stop other work; 'avg reaction' = hours from blocker creation to the blocked issue reaching In Progress, 'stagnation' = % of blocked targets stuck >24h (higher = more blocked pipeline). <b>B · Process Rework</b> (causes / is caused by) — 'escaped causes' = defects created AFTER their source issue was already closed (rework that should have been caught earlier). <b>C · Scope Duplication</b> (duplicates / clones / Cloners) — 'sunk hours' = time spent In Progress on issues later closed as Duplicate/Won't Fix (wasted effort); 'closed dupes' = count of such issues. <b>D · Soft Associations</b> (relates to / Related To / Part of) — 'closure sync' = % of linked pairs closed within the same month (higher = better coordinated delivery). The doughnut shows the share of each category among all links; each callout card reports the key metric for its category.
